clue.text: Revelling heading North from Brazil?

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is Brazil's best-known city, so the query stands for RIO
a trip heading north from Brazil goes to the US, giving TO US

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person on a northbound journey out of Brazil is off to celebrate.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as a journey: from RIO, TO US. The question mark flags that Brazil stands for its city.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a riotous party is one full of noisy, wild celebration.

clue.text: Strong vehicle covered in decay

indicators.note: covered in means the vehicle sits inside the decay

parts.note: rot is decay
a bus is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A sturdy vehicle has been left to go rusty.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something sturdy and vigorous is strong.

clue.text: Old and bald, maladjusted and eccentric

indicators.note: maladjusted means badly arranged, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A description of an old, bald man who is unsettled and peculiar.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'and' joining Old and bald is a link; 'maladjusted' scrambles both words together.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an odd, unconventional person is an eccentric.

clue.text: Open about cry of deterrence? That's to go too far

indicators.note: about means the open word goes round the cry

parts.note: overt means open, not hidden
shoo is the cry used to drive off an animal

explanation.surface: Someone opens up about a warning shout and is accused of going too far.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to overshoot a target is to go past or beyond it.

clue.text: Unusually extended action has economy heading for doldrums in an instant

parts.note: the splits is a gymnastic move with the legs stretched wide
econ is a short form of economy or economics

indicators.note: heading for takes the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: An economic stretch is heading into a slump in no time at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a fraction of a second is a mere instant.

clue.text: Claim associated with scoundrel remains

indicators.note: associated with simply sets the two pieces side by side, the scoundrel leading

parts.note: a cad is a dishonourable man, a scoundrel
to aver is to claim or assert

explanation.surface: A rogue's claim is linked to what was left behind, perhaps in a dispute over an estate.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer puts the scoundrel first though the clue names the claim first.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a corpse is a person's mortal remains.

clue.text: Runs from bird or animal

indicators.note: from means the runs letter is taken out of the bird

parts.note: a crow is a bird
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: Something flees from a bird or a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Runs' looks like the verb, but it is the letter R being removed.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a farm animal kept for milk.

clue.text: Protest British post-war activity?

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A British protest held after the war ended.
explanation.walkthrough: Demobilisation, soldiers being released from the forces, is what happens after a war.
explanation.definitionFit: Short form: discharging troops once fighting ends is what happens after a war.

clue.text: Very excited to acquire new hot artist

indicators.note: to acquire means the excited word takes in the new letter

parts.note: agog means eagerly excited
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: An enthusiastic fan is thrilled to buy work by a fashionable new painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Vincent was a Dutch post-impressionist painter.

clue.text: Fruit came up — chap's bringing in first of plums

parts.note: rose is the past tense of rise, came up

indicators.note: bringing in means the possessive word takes in the plum letter

parts.note: his means belonging to a chap

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Fruit appeared, and a man brings in the first plums of the season.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the red berries of wild roses are a fruit.

clue.text: Sleeping partner's aggrieved response about Fed getting involved

indicators.note: about means the roar goes round the other letters

parts.note: an angry or wounded roar is a bellow

indicators.note: getting involved means the letters of Fed are tangled up into a new order

explanation.surface: A partner in bed grumbles loudly about the Federal Reserve meddling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting involved' makes DFE from Fed, and 'about' wraps BELLOW round it after BE.
explanation.definitionFit: Literal sense: the person you share a bed with, also used for an associate or ally.

clue.text: Repairs pieces and shards at last

parts.note: chess pieces are called men

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of each of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Someone puts broken pottery back together from its pieces and shards.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, as verbs: to repair something is to fix it up.

clue.text: Stops time? Makes a comment about that

indicators.note: about means the commenting word is placed round the time letter

parts.note: to make a comment is to say something

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether time can be halted, and another remarks on that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' points back to time, the piece the comment goes round.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, as verbs: to stay an execution or a process is to halt it.

clue.text: Where you queue to pay also involving lines taking hours

indicators.note: taking means the next piece is added on at the end
involving means the phrase for also encloses the lines

parts.note: the idiom 'to boot' means also or in addition
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A description of a road checkpoint where drivers wait for ages, crossing lanes to hand over a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'also' wants to be TOO, but here it is the idiom 'to boot', which 'involving' splits open.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a kiosk on a road or bridge where drivers line up to hand over a charge.

clue.text: Mixed hypo alright for print-making

indicators.note: mixed means the letters of hypo alright are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: Mixing fixing solution for a photographic or printing process.
explanation.walkthrough: Hypo is sodium thiosulphate, a fixer in photography, which suits the printing surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: printing from a flat stone or plate is a method of print-making.

clue.text: Completely finished, he's initially happy amongst best, having no idea where he's headed?

definitions.text: having no idea where he's headed?

parts.note: something completely finished is all over

indicators.note: amongst means these letters go in among the letters of best

parts.note: top means best, as in top quality
he's gives its letters with the apostrophe dropped

indicators.note: initially means the first letter of the following word is taken

explanation.surface: A man, finished and yet cheerful among his betters, wanders without direction.
explanation.walkthrough: THE SHOP comes from TOP (best) with HES and H (happy's first letter) placed amongst it.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: being in total disarray, scattered everywhere, is like someone without any sense of direction.

clue.text: Arrangement for lutes involving work for singer covering the mouth

indicators.note: involving means the rearranged letters enclose the singer's piece
arrangement for means the letters of lutes are rearranged

parts.note: an aria is a solo piece for a singer

explanation.surface: A musical arrangement for lutes with a song in which the singer covers their mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arrangement for' gives ESTUL, which 'involving' wraps round ARIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjective sense: relating to an estuary, the wide mouth of a river.

clue.text: Not quite par? Golfer unexpectedly to jump forward

indicators.note: unexpectedly means the letters are thrown into a surprising order
not quite means the final letter of par is left off

explanation.surface: A golfer just misses par and suddenly jumps up the leaderboard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims PAR to PA; 'unexpectedly' scrambles PA with GOLFER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, as verbs: to vault over others and get ahead is to jump forward.

clue.text: Position of sun? Quite often I'm confused about area, with nothing further to add in

indicators.note: confused means the letters of these three words, plus the extra ones, are jumbled
about means the jumbled words are placed around the area letter, so it joins the mix
further to add in means one more letter is slipped in among the words being jumbled

parts.note: nothing is zero, written as the letter O

explanation.surface: Someone frequently gets muddled about an area and has nothing more to contribute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' scrambles QUITE OFTEN I'M; 'about' puts that round A, and 'further to add in' slips O in too, so all fourteen letters end up in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomy term: the difference between sundial time and clock time, which tracks where the sun appears relative to mean time.

clue.text: Place to study bad jokes, the point of which has never been perceived

definitions.text: the point of which has never been perceived

parts.note: uni is short for university, a place to study
corn is trite, corny humour

explanation.surface: A university with dreadful jokes whose point nobody has ever seen.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'point' is not a joke's meaning but a horn that no one has ever seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cryptic description: this mythical beast has a single horn, a point no one has ever actually seen.

clue.text: Europeans picked up 25 down in publications

indicators.note: in means the turned letters go inside the publications

parts.note: mags are magazines, publications

indicators.note: picked up in a down clue means the letters are read upwards

parts.note: the answer to 25 down is a beam of sunlight

explanation.surface: Europeans spotted a cross-reference in some magazines.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'picked up' means read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Hungarians, the dominant people of Hungary, are Europeans.

clue.text: Whiskey in container on the old still

indicators.note: on means the container comes first, with the old word placed after

parts.note: a pot is a container
e'en is an archaic contraction of even, which means still

explanation.surface: Whiskey held in a container on top of an old distilling apparatus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' looks like a distillery's apparatus but is the adverb, 'even', in its old form.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an Irish illicit spirit distilled from potatoes or grain is a kind of whiskey.

clue.text: Flirt casually addressing ruling couple?

parts.note: Phil is the casual way to address Prince Philip
and is the word that couples things together
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the reigning queen

explanation.surface: A cheeky courtier addresses the King and Queen informally, verging on flirting.
explanation.walkthrough: The ruling couple was Prince Philip and Queen Elizabeth: casually, Phil and ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, as verbs: to dally with many partners is to flirt.

clue.text: A key part of the theatre

parts.note: a key or cay is a small island, an isle

explanation.surface: An important element of a theatre is named.
explanation.walkthrough: 'key' looks like 'important' but is a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the walkway between rows of seats is part of a theatre.

clue.text: Old King, in past, threatening action

indicators.note: in means the king's letters sit inside the word for past

parts.note: something in the past happened long ago
GR is Georgius Rex, King George, a former monarch

explanation.surface: An ancient monarch, long ago, took aggressive action.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang for aggressive, intimidating behaviour or trouble-making.

clue.text: Contents of house and home mostly having money invested

indicators.note: invested means money is placed inside, as in a fund
mostly means the last letter of the word for home is dropped

parts.note: a roost is a bird's home or resting place

explanation.surface: A householder's possessions and home are largely funded by invested cash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' cuts ROOST to ROOS; 'invested' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a house is made up of its chambers, so they are what it contains.

clue.text: Copy salesman, having story about pet

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: about means the story wraps round the pet

parts.note: a lie is a made-up story
a cat is a common household pet

explanation.surface: A salesman spins a yarn about a pet in order to imitate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym, as verbs: to duplicate something exactly is to copy it.

clue.text: Very wet, not in a bit of sun

indicators.note: not means the letters of in are removed from the wet word

parts.note: rainy weather is very wet

explanation.surface: It is very wet, with not a glimmer of sunshine.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a single beam of light from the sun is a small bit of it.

clue.text: Use of artillery sees grand religious building losing facade

parts.note: G is a common abbreviation for grand, a thousand pounds

indicators.note: losing facade means the front letter of the building is removed

parts.note: a nunnery is a convent, a religious house

explanation.surface: Shelling damages a grand convent so that its frontage is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the operation and firing of heavy guns is artillery work.

clue.text: Russian leader still wrong about Left

indicators.note: about means the word for still goes round the left letter

parts.note: yet means still, as in 'not yet'
a sin is a wrong

explanation.surface: A Russian leader remains mistaken about the political Left.
explanation.walkthrough: Boris Yeltsin was Russia's first president.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the first president of post-Soviet Russia was this leader.
